title: Multipart media uploads stop before availability
summary: Large media uploads remain in a pending state and do not appear in the asset browser, while smaller uploads complete normally.
precursor: A partner began uploading high-resolution campaign footage through the resumable upload endpoint during a regional traffic peak.
impact: Editors cannot review newly uploaded footage, and clients retrying the same uploads increase ingest traffic.

title: Tenant media cleanup leaves deleted assets visible
summary: Offboarded tenant assets remain listed after cleanup, and repeated cleanup attempts report failures for the same batch.
precursor: A tenant offboarding workflow started removing catalog records while a retention worker was processing associated renditions.
impact: Former tenant content continues to consume catalog and storage capacity, and the offboarding workflow cannot be confirmed complete.

title: Image rendition workers stop making progress
summary: Preview generation stops advancing beyond a small group of recent uploads, even though workers remain healthy and online.
precursor: A studio bulk-imported a mixed set of camera originals, after which rendition jobs for later uploads began cycling through retries.
impact: New images lack thumbnails in review screens, slowing approval and leaving editors unable to distinguish recent uploads.

title: Archived video downloads fail for selected recordings
summary: Download requests for a subset of older recordings fail, while their catalog entries and neighboring recordings remain accessible.
precursor: The archive team completed a lifecycle-tier migration for recordings older than ninety days earlier in the day.
impact: Support staff cannot retrieve affected footage for customer requests, and the archive inventory no longer matches the records shown to users.

title: Replaced media continues serving an earlier rendition
summary: Some viewers continue to receive the prior version of a replaced image, although the asset page shows the new upload as current.
precursor: An editor replaced approved product photography shortly before a scheduled catalog publication, and delivery traffic rose as the catalog went live.
impact: Customers see inconsistent product imagery across sessions and storefront regions, creating review churn and risking incorrect merchandising.
